exp/legibility — object legibility from markings: rectangles, in 2D, on box faces

Branch exp/legibility off main @ 5d8eb46 (the full renderer-v3 pipeline including phase 4's finishes and detail layer). The maintainer's ask, verbatim: "I think I'd prioritize object legibility to start … in the manager's office, the monitor looks great but the keyboard doesn't. similarly, the cardboard boxes are hard to recognize. same for vending machine. are there very simple textures that we'd use judiciously across our objects to make them more recognizable?" — then the strategic intent: "see how much we can push into textures and OUT OF GEOMETRY to speed up our rendering pipeline; curious how well this works with everything we're doing (e.g. RT reflections)". The answer built here: legibility at follow-camera distance comes from one or two signifiers per object class made of the same thing the world is made of — rectangles, in 2D, ON a face — as a tiny palette-indexed bitmap per marking, authored image-style (generators for key grids / seams / text bars / LED rows / can rows, ASCII art for the this-side-up glyphs and labels) and rendered analytically on a world-space texel lattice. Short version of the verdict, ahead of the pictures: at follow height on high the keyboard, the cartons and the two vending machines now read as what they are (§2, the verdict rows); the whole set costs nothing measurable at any tier (≤ one 65 µs timer quantum, §7); with everything off the frame is main's, hash for hash (§8); an emissive marking is a real light and the meter in front of the vending window reads what it read in front of the old glowing slab (§6); the geometry demotion took the office from 925 to 772 boxes but — honestly — saved no ray time, because nearly all the relief it replaced was already raster-only (§9).

The hard rules this was built and judged under (the maintainer's, verbatim where quoted)

  • The KEYBOARD must read as a keyboard at follow height — it is a headline object beside the cartons and the vending machine: a single slab box + a cap / gap grid on the base lattice, a longer space-bar run, a slightly lighter cap colour than the deck. Verdict row at follow height ×1 / ×3, then close-up, five tiers (§2, §3).
  • NO GRADIENTS anywhere in a marking — flat colour per texel, ≤ 3 colours (a palette entry per marking is a MATERIAL: albedo — absolute, or × the box's own — roughness, emitted radiance). The one place with more than three lit hues is the vending window (three entries: two product colours + the backlight; the rails are the machine's own body showing through the transparent cells).
  • NO BAKED LIGHTING of any kind — no painted shadows, no faux-AO in seams beyond the flat seam colour, no bevels on key caps, no vignettes: a marking writes albedo / roughness / genuine emission only, so every bit of shading on it comes from the real lights (a moving torch, the mirror floors, the light meter). With the palette holding materials rather than shaded colours this is impossible by construction — there is no field to put a shadow in (§1; the albedo-view crops in §5 show the flat cells). Nothing authored had to be flattened: the first cut already had no depth edges or vignettes.
  • "Simple enough — low resolution, intentionally kinda like pixel art — so it doesn't draw attention to how it's a flat texture": ONE world-space base texel (MARKING_TEXEL 2.5 cm) with a nesting ladder fine = 1.25 cm / coarse = 5 cm per marking; every rect / grid line / glyph cell snaps to its lattice; anti-aliasing only at cell boundaries; under ~1 output pixel per cell a marking fades to a local, then global, mean instead of aliasing (§1, §4).
  • Never demote a free-standing object to a marking on the surface under it, however thin — papers, notes, books, trays keep their boxes ("the sheet's edge is what makes it a thing on the table"); markings go ON objects (papers get grey text bars, one gets a scribble); what may be demoted is only relief that belongs to a face (§9).
tiles: — crops of the OUTPUT frame (1777×1000 at high) upscaled ×3 nearest at capture (so "×3" tiles are 3 output px per screen px at zoom ×1); scroll a strip sideways. 1. What was built — the representation, the shader, the rules in numbers

Representation (image-style authoring, analytic rendering). A marking = { face, res, at: [U0, V0], size: [W, H] ≤ 32×32, pal: ≤ 3 material entries, cells: H strings of W chars from ". a b c" } — a 2-bit-per-cell bitmap whose bottom-left cell sits at integer lattice coordinates (U0, V0) from the FACE CENTRE along the face's (u = right, v = up seen from outside; on ±y u = +x, v = ∓z) axes, cell size = 2.5 cm × ½ / 1 / 2 (fine / base / coarse, all nesting on the same face). A palette entry is a material: albedo (absolute linear rgb) or mul (× the box's own albedo), rough (absent = the box's), emit (radiance rgb). ≤ 4 markings per box (BoxData.markings / PropPartData.markings in the level file, validated: keys, enums, the bitmap inside its face, cell alphabet ≤ palette length; canonical serialize; both load directions; the level identity probe compares them leaf for leaf). Procedural kinds are generators (scene/markings.ts GEN.grid / seams / lines / scribble / dots / window / glyph painting a CellCanvas); hand-drawn kinds are ASCII art in scene/markingDefaults.ts. The office's per-KIND defaults live there (keyboard, monitor UI bars, carton tape + print + label, shelf cartons, filing cabinet, cupboards, binder, book run, papers, sheets, whiteboard, both vending machines, keypad, extinguisher / cabinet / cylinder, rack vents + LEDs, door leaf plates, clock, lobby sign, placard, plate / LED / display helpers, pallet deck, first-aid cross) and officeGen.ts calls them at the object sites, so levels/office.json carries every marking explicitly (243 KB → 251 KB with cells; 149 records / 1.7 k table rows at run time). Two examples as stored:

  aaaaaaaaaaaaaa   b = cap   albedo 0.15   rough 0.45          a.a.a..bbbbb                                     a........a.a

                                                               aaaaa.......                                     aaaaaaaaaaaa

GPU. No image, no texture binding, no sampling in any ray pass. The table lives in the tail of the existing boxMat storage buffer (no new binding anywhere — the fragment stages were at 9 of Metal's 10): a record = 8 header vec4 rows (where / which face / res, coverage fractions, three material entries) + ⌈W·H / 48⌉ cell rows (12 cells per float as an exact small integer — no bit pattern a float load could renormalise). A box's first record row rides in the top 14 bits of its GPU flags word (bits 18‥31; the glass probe now asserts they are set exactly on marked boxes); the secondary rays read a 4th mat row = the box albedo with the markings' area average folded in on the CPU (§10). Frame uniform +16 B (markCfg @688: base texel — 0 = off everywhere —, contrast, emission ×, evaluate-at-reflection-hits; frame-layout probe green, materials-frame compares the first 688 B against main's writeFrame). Evaluation (render/shaders/markings.wgsl):

  • g-buffer (fsBox, after the detail layer, before the encounter's decals): box-local position + face from the flat normal; per record on this face: cell coords = face uv ÷ texel − (U0, V0); the pixel footprint per axis from dpdx/dpdy of the world position (taken in uniform control flow, rotated into the face); the two nearest cells per axis blended by the footprint's analytic coverage of the boundary between them — a hard step at zero footprint, a one-cell ramp at one cell per pixel — so AA exists only at cell edges and is stable under the TAAU jitter (three consecutive frames at low: tile mean luma 139.51 / 139.56 / 139.53); writes albedo (entries with an albedo lerp from the pixel's own by contrast) and roughness. Minification: past 0.75 cells per pixel the taps fade to the plain box average of the ≤ 4×4 cells under the footprint (a LOCAL mean: a row of LEDs stays a row of dim dots), past ~3 cells per pixel to the record's global coverage fractions × how much of the footprint the bitmap covers (a tint, never noise).
  • composite adds the emission of emissive entries at the primary hit (× the box's markGain — the switchable's supply, so a blackout / the OCP / a flicker take the vending window and a monitor's UI bars down with the fixture — × emissiveScale), so it blooms and reads in NV like a fixture. reflect.wgsl / reflect_p5.wgsl evaluate the hit box's markings at reflection hits (albedo + emission), band-limited by a cone = the receiver pixel's footprint + 2α × hit distance (§10). Gather / cascade / probe hits never evaluate cells: they read the folded albedo row.
  • Legibility arithmetic. Follow camera: pitch 55°, distance 21 m, vertical fov 28°, 1000 output rows at high → 1.05 cm per output pixel across the view; on a desk top 1.05 × 1.28 cm per px, on a vertical face facing the camera 1.05 × 1.83. So one base cell (2.5 cm) is ≈ 2.4 × 2.0 output px on tops and 2.4 × 1.4 on fronts (over the 1.5 px floor); a fine cell is 1.2 × 1.0 (under it: only for close cameras — it fades toward its mean at follow height, mostly on the lower tiers); a coarse cell 4.8 × 4. Internally at high (0.77 scale, 770 rows) a base cell is 1.84 px, at medium 1.44, at low 1.03, at verylow 0.71 (→ the mean: the keyboard is a grey slab with a lighter middle at verylow, §3).

2. The verdict rows — BEFORE (main's office, ?level=relief) vs AFTER at follow-camera height, then the close showcase angle

Every pair is the same staged deterministic frame (guards parked dark, Sam invisible, phases zeroed, 26–30 settled renders at high 1368×770 → 1777×1000): the game camera's own pitch 55° / distance 21 m / fov 28° looking at the object ("follow"), cropped ×3 nearest (and ×1 for the three headline objects), then a closer angle. Left / first = before, right / second = after.

Keyboard on the manager's desk under the desk lamp

verdict: reads as a keyboard at ×1 and ×3 — two rows of caps + the space-bar run on a near-black deck; the papers beside it get their bars. In the dark monitor above it the key grid shows again, mirrored (RT reflections at a screen's 0.08 roughness).

Cartons on the storage floor under the bare bulb (+ the shelf cartons behind)

verdict: read as shipping cartons — the brown tape band over the top seam and down the near face is the signifier that works at 21 m; the fine print (this-side-up arrows + fragile glass) survives as small dark marks low on the faces and reads fully from ~8 m in. First cut had light kraft tape: invisible at follow height, changed to brown.

Cartons against the cubicles' west partition (moonlit, mostly dark)

verdict: tape reads where any light reaches; in the unlit corner nothing does — markings are albedo: no light, no signifier (by the rules). The recycling box (blue) has no tape by design.

The two vending machines in the break room, front (they face south), the room dark as at night

verdict: instantly two vending machines — A (left) the drinks machine: four shelves of tall bottles in the machine's red + dark cola against a warm red backlight, a lit button column, flap and coin panel; B the snack machine: seven shelves of packets in blue / orange, tags, a keypad block (real 3 cm box, fine key grid), bin + coin return. Before: two uniform glowing slabs.

Their image in the break-room lino (rough 0.22)

verdict: the windows land in the floor as soft red / blue lobes hardening toward the contact, through the reflection pass evaluating the emissive marking at its hits (band-limited by the lino's cone: no can structure in the lobe, physically right) plus the registered light's analytic image.

The filing cabinets against the corridor partition (drawers face the cubicles)

verdict: three drawers each, seams + pulls (coarse 5 cm cells: a seam is 5 cm — chunky and legible; replaces nine NoShadow pull-strip boxes).

Papers on a cubicle desk

verdict: documents, not white slabs — grey bars a cell tall, ragged, a paragraph break; the sheets keep their boxes and their edge shadow.

Conference-room whiteboard (marker writing in two muted colours + a green scribble; the sticky notes stay boxes)

verdict: reads as a used whiteboard; the three stroke boxes it had are demoted into these markings.

Server-room door, corridor face (dim: one corridor panel lit)

verdict: kick plate + push plate are there and correct, but a stainless plate on a dark leaf in a dark corridor is a low-contrast signifier — it reads when a torch or the panel catches its lower roughness (0.32 vs the leaf's 0.55), which is the physically honest version.

Extinguisher on the corridor wall west of the server door

verdict: the white label band makes the red cylinder an extinguisher rather than a red post (70 output px tall at follow height; the band is 3 of them).

Server racks, west bank, LED faces

verdict: the LED rows read exactly as the old emissive nubs did (fine dots, the amber fault light included; 96 boxes gone) — after the local-mean minification fix: the first cut smeared each LED bitmap into a green bar at follow height. The vent grille on the lower doors is subtle by intent (texture of the metal).

Three binders stood on a cubicle desk

verdict: white spine labels visible up close; at follow height three 6 cm spines are 6 px each — the labels are a couple of pixels: they help a little, the silhouette does the work.

3. Five tiers at follow height — does it degrade to a tint, does it crawl?

ultra 2133×1200 · high 1368×770 → 1777×1000 · medium 1072×603 → 1600×900 · low 768×432 → 1280×720 · verylow 533×300 → 1066×600 (each crop is the same region of its own output frame ×3, so the tiles shrink with the output). Keyboard: keys distinct at ultra / high, visible at medium, key rows soft at low, a grey slab with a lighter interior at verylow — a tint, no noise, as designed. Vending: the coarse windows read at every tier. Shimmer: three consecutive frames of the keyboard tile at low (below, ×4) — mean luma 139.51 / 139.56 / 139.53, no crawl by eye: the AA is analytic against the lattice, so the TAAU jitter moves nothing.

Recommendation: keep 2.5 cm as the base. 2 cm buys the keyboard a third row and is still (just) over the pixel at high, but everything base-lattice drops to 1.5 px at medium and under a pixel at low — the whole set would live in the minification fade on the tiers most players get; 4 cm is right for big things (it is what coarse already gives the cabinet fronts, kick plates and vending windows) and wrong for desk objects. The ladder does the real work: desk objects on base, carton print / LEDs / clock hands / keypads on fine (accepting they are close-camera detail), fronts over 0.8 m on coarse. Does the fine carton print earn its keep at play distance? Partly: after the local-mean fix the arrows + glass survive at 21 m as small dark marks that say "printed carton" without being legible; the tape does the recognising. I would keep the print (it costs nothing and pays off whenever the camera comes in — the tour, a zoom, the breach) and not add more of it.

5. The vending corner: night, lit, the mirror, direct-only, and the flat cells

These are the FIRST-CUT machines (multi-hue can windows) as reviewed; they were restyled on 08-10 — §10b has the red / blue single-chroma machines, their reflections and the reflection-path fixes. Kept here as the record of what the maintainer reacted to.

The product window is the one emissive marking that matters, so it gets its own checks: at night (the room's panels off, as the level starts) the windows are the corner's light; with the break-room panels on they sit in a lit room without blowing out; the bloom is the same modest halo the old slabs had (the windows are calibrated to the old slabs' luminous intensity over nearly the same area, so their mean radiance — what bloom and tone mapping see — is about where it was: peaks 3.1 (A, red) / 1.75 (B, blue) W/sr/m² per channel against the old flat 2.6 / 2.8). The direct-only view shows the two registered lights laying red and blue light on the lino and the west wall — the marking's light is in the direct pass like any fixture. The albedo view shows what a marking is made of: flat cells, three materials, nothing shaded.

6. Emissive markings ARE lights (the one-model rule)

Any marking entry with emit on a switchable's box registers a one-sided rectangular emitter over its bitmap exactly as an emissive fixture box does (game.ts: radiance × area → on-axis intensity, the disc never wider than the rect's short side, 7 cm proud of the face, in the target's areaLights so lighting.ts drives it with the supply; the marking is then flagged area-lit so a reflection ray takes only emitTraceK of its traced radiance and the analytic image carries the rest — one window either way). Below an on-axis intensity of 0.05 nothing registers (LED rows 0.01, a monitor's UI bars 0.02, the drinks machine's buttons 0.002 — they glow on screen and in mirrors only, as the raster-only nubs they replace did; the dimmest real fixture light on the floor is an exit sign at 0.46). The office registers exactly two: vending 2.28 and vending2 1.29 W/sr — the light list has the same count as main's (the old slab lights were 2.84 / 2.22 on the peak channel; the windows are calibrated on luminous intensity because their light is whiter than the pure red / blue slabs — matched on the peak channel the meter read a third more). ReSTIR shadows, froxel beams, the bounce and the light meter see them because they are lights, full stop.

Proof — the light meter (the irradiance probe at Sam's chest / head, W/m², guards parked, torches off; before = ?level=relief = main's slabs, after = the windows):

8. Identity — everything off = main, hash for hash; the level identity gate

  • ?level=relief&nomarkings vs main @ 5d8eb46 served from a scratch worktree, the P4 harness's deterministic still (__p4.identityHash: seeded dice, parked guards, zeroed phases, __resetClock, 40 frames + one offscreen render, FNV over the RGBA readback): high cubicles 56247efe = 56247efe, vending e4e919fe = e4e919fe, storage aa8e482f = aa8e482f; medium cubicles 8109c591 = 8109c591, vending 290932a4 = 290932a4. What the branch changes on that path and why none of it reaches a pixel: the mat rows are 4 vec4 a box instead of 3 (same numbers, other addresses; the g-buffer's previous-transform index follows), the Frame is 704 B with markCfg.x = 0, fsBox takes two derivatives it never uses and a branch it never enters, composite / the reflection passes test a slot that is 0, the seven secondary-hit sites read boxAlbedoSec = the same three floats as boxAlbedo, door leaves carry marking data the upload ignores.
  • Level. levels/office-relief.json (generator with { markings: false, demote: false }) is byte-identical to main's levels/office.json (digest 7168ed9858f17); the new levels/office.json is what the generator writes by default (digest ed51c1e88d6e6): probes.ts level — generator ≡ file 0 diffs, digest three ways equal, not stale, canonical, validator + planted faults + round trip ALL PASS.
  • Gates (this tree): typecheck clean · tools/qa/gate.sh perf frame-layout level materials player glass: exit 0 — perf 24/0 · frame-layout 9/0 · level all PASS · materials 43/0 · player 166/0 · glass 39/0 · tour.ts --runs 1: 1/1 PASS (13 stops, Sam never hit) · soak.ts --seeds 2 --minutes 4: 0 violations · bun run build: exit 0 · GPU validation (an error scope + the uncaptured list across the five presets × markings on / off × debug views 0 / 1 / 14 / 15): 0 errors.

9. Geometry → markings: the rule, what moved per room, what it saved (honestly: box count yes, ray time no)

The rule (the maintainer's, applied): NEVER demote a free-standing object to a marking on the surface under it, however thin — papers, folders, notes, books, trays, mats keep their boxes (the sheet's edge shadow / its offset from the desk is what makes it a thing on the table); markings go ON objects (papers get text bars, one gets a scribble; whiteboards get marker strokes; the keyboard keeps its one slab and gets the key grid). What MAY be demoted is only RELIEF THAT BELONGS TO A FACE — sub-part boxes whose removal deletes no object: pull strips flush on a drawer front, LED nubs, glow / trim strips, screen sheets flush on a housing, door-gap strips, deck boards, painted marks modelled as 2 mm boxes.

What it saved, measured. Boxes per trace-grid cell (parked stage, same both ways): items 2775 → 2761 (−0.5 %), max per cell 18 → 18, cubicles mean 4.04 → 4.04, storage 4.89 → 4.89, server 3.63 → 3.63, break room 1.84 → 1.81, empty cells 349 → 349. Serialized medians at high, relief → demoted: cubicles overview direct 2.425 → 2.490, gather 1.901 → 1.901, reflect 0.131 → 0.131, union 7.93 → 7.93; vending follow direct 2.163 → 2.163, gather 1.507 → 1.442, reflect 0.328 → 0.328, softblur 0.983 → 0.918, union 7.47 → 7.34 (−0.13, the two slabs out of the break room's busiest cells — one quantum territory). The stress minute (QRF + rain + two canisters, no fight, 150 serialized frames orbiting at high, 41 lights): Σ compute p50 10.81 → 10.22 ms, direct 3.15 → 3.08, gather 2.16 → 1.90, reflect 0.26 → 0.26 (the 'before' take drew the maintainer's frames — its p95 was 17.8 ms against 10.6 — so read the gather column as contention, not a saving; direct and reflect agree with the calm views). So: no ray-time speed-up from this pass, and the reason is instructive — 146 of the 153 boxes it removed were authored NoShadow (raster-only relief: never in the trace grid, so no ray ever paid for them) and the seven traced ones (the vending slabs, the pallet boards) sit in cells nothing expensive crosses. The office was already lean where rays go. What the system buys instead is the strategic thing: future dressing detail — legends, labels, panels, grilles, seams — now costs zero rays and zero boxes, reads in the RT reflections and the light meter by construction, and the raster list is 18 % shorter (upload / motion-vector snapshot / instance count, all under the timer's resolution here).

10. Markings at reflection hits, and the GI fold

Reflection hits (reflect.wgsl / reflect_p5.wgsl shadeReflHit + reflHitParts; restir / denoise / froxel / taau / volumetrics untouched): the hit box's markings on the hit face are composited into the hit albedo and their emission added, band-limited by a cone footprint = the receiver pixel's own footprint + 2α × hit distance (α = roughness²) instead of derivatives — so the keyboard two metres off in the lino (rough 0.22) is its mean colour, and in the manager's dark screen (0.08) at arm's length it is keys (§2's last close-up); the vending windows in the lino are the soft lobes of §5. Cost of the reflect pass at high on the vending view: 0.328 → 0.328 ms (one quantum on the cubicles view: 0.066 → 0.131). Switch: settings.markingReflect / Tab row.

Gather / cascade / probe hits do NOT evaluate cells. Each marked box's albedo for the secondary rays is its own albedo + Σ over its markings of (mean albedo change × bitmap area ÷ the box's total surface), computed once on the CPU when the list is packed (markings.ts secondaryAlbedo → the 4th mat row → boxAlbedoSec at the seven secondary-hit sites in fgather / lighting_common / cards) — the same energy the per-pixel evaluation returns averaged over the box, at zero ray-path cost. Emission needs no fold: the emissive markings that matter are registered lights (their box is not flagged Emissive, so no gather ray double counts them — exactly the AreaLit rule), and the LED-class ones replace NoShadow nubs no ray ever saw. Check: the indirect-only view (debug 4) of the break room from the follow camera, 8-bit luma means, main's geometry vs the marked level: the lino tile in front of the machines 19.66 → 19.51 (−0.7 %), the whole visible room 14.46 → 14.22 (−1.6 %) — against a run-to-run wander of ±1 % on the same tile (19.77 / 19.51 in two default takes): unchanged within the gather's own noise.

10b. Follow-up (08-10): “the markings don’t show up in the glossy reflections — like the vending machine?” — the diagnosis, two fixes, two rules, the restyled machines

What the maintainer saw: the vending windows mirrored in the break-room lino as featureless glowing lobes (§5) — none of the pixel art. The lead’s diagnosis from reading the shaders, both confirmed in the code: (1) a double blur — markReflHit band-limited the art at a traced hit by a cone growing 2α per metre (α = rough²), but the reflection RAYS are already drawn from the GGX lobe and the specular denoiser averages them, so the lobe was applied twice; (2) the emissive split — the window is a registered rectangular light, so on a rough receiver reflect.wgsl takes 1 − emitTraceK(rough) of its image through the ANALYTIC highlight, which knows the rectangle and not the art: a uniform panel. (3) Nothing else gates them off: markCfg.w is on by default, the vending bodies are statics (not props) and every box — static or dynamic — takes its slot bits through the one upload loop; reflect_p5.wgsl carries the same lines at ultra.

What measuring added (before touching anything): at this view the visible blur is neither of those — it is the lobe itself. The raw traced signal (history 1, no à-trous; first crop) is a cloud of one-ray dots with no structure at any cone setting, and cone 0 / 0.25α / 2α render identically after the denoiser (next row): on 0.22 lino, α = 0.048, the reflected lobe’s median radius is ≈ 9.6 cm per metre of mirror path (p80 ≈ 20 cm) — a 16 cm can pitch cannot survive past ~0.4 m of path, and the window’s bottom edge already sat 0.3 m above the floor. The old slab looked “sharp” only because a uniform rectangle has nothing to lose but its edge. So the two fixes below are right and cheap, but what actually puts a machine’s design INTO a satin floor is design at the scale the lobe passes: large luminance structure (a control-column notch, a ribbon, a roundel) — which is where the maintainer’s restyle landed anyway.

Fix 1 — the traced-hit cone is the pixel’s ray cone + a small share of the lobe

markings.wgsl: fp(t) = fp₀ + t·(cpix + k·α), where fp₀ = the receiver pixel’s footprint, cpix = its angular size (a planar mirror keeps the primary cone diverging at the same rate — this term was missing) and k = settings.markingReflCone, default 0.25 (was a hard 2.0): the rays + the denoiser realise the lobe; the per-hit prefilter only trades a little bias for one-ray noise. Tab ▸ Renderer — markings ▸ ‘reflection-hit cone’, __mark.set({cone}). The three settings side by side, everything else fixed (after the restyle, high, ×3):

Identical to the eye at this distance, as predicted: with 90 % of the signal traced, the lobe (realised by the ray distribution) dominates any per-hit prefilter. The knob matters on polish at short mirror paths (a keyboard in a screen at arm’s length), where 2α·t was still small — which is why nothing looked wrong there either.

Fix 2 — the analytic highlight of a marking’s light is textured with the marking (flux-conserving)

An area light registered for an emissive marking now carries a link to it (lights.ts RtLight.markRef = box « 2 | ordinal, in the kind word’s bits 11‥24, bit 10 = present; common.wgsl lightMarkRef). In rtGlints’ kind-3 branch (both reflect modules) the light’s uniform, lobe-convolved image is multiplied by markPatternAtMirror: the marking’s emission at the point where the receiver’s MIRROR ray meets the marking’s plane, ÷ (the record’s mean emission × the footprint’s coverage of the bitmap), band-limited by the pixel cone + the WHOLE lobe (2α per metre — the analytic image has no ray distribution to realise the blur, so its texture takes all of it), clamped 0‥6, handed back to 1 as the overlap thins. Extent and fall-off stay the lobe’s D (coverage is divided back out); only the relative pattern is imprinted, so its mean over the window is 1 — flux-neutral by construction. A/B switch: settings.markingReflPattern (Tab ‘A/B: textured analytic highlight’; the sign of frame.markCfg.w — no Frame growth, still 704 B).

On this floor the textured analytic share is a 10 % term under a 90 % traced one, so the first pair differ by a shade in the notch and in the ribbon’s glow; on a worn lane at rough 0.3 (kEmit 0.35) it is two-thirds of the image. The third crop is the honest measure of how much of the reflection is the marking at all: nearly all of it.

The two rules (the maintainer’s), now stated in the code and held by construction

FLUX. An emissive marking redistributes radiance across its face but integrates to its registered light: the kind-3 rectangle is DERIVED from the pattern (colour = mean chroma, intensity = luminance-calibrated radiance × area), the box’s own emissive is zero, and every visual path draws the pattern itself — the g-buffer + composite at the primary hit (markEmissiveAt, nothing added on top of the light), traced reflection hits (markReflHit × kEmit), the analytic highlight (× pattern ÷ mean). Illumination, shadows, froxels, GI and the light meter read only the rectangle. Numerically (high, the lino tile under the machines, direct-only view, mean 8-bit luma): pattern textured 94.99 · uniform 95.01 · markings not drawn at all 95.02 — identical to 0.03 %; the chest meter 1 m in front of machine A 3.219 / 3.216 W/m², between the machines 0.4394 / 0.4370, room middle 0.1013 / 0.1010 (the far control spot wanders 0.045‥0.049 with the gather’s own noise).
ONE CHROMA per emitter. An emitting bitmap keeps one hue and redistributes LUMINANCE only — the dominant colour, its light tint / white, a dark — because ONE rectangular light stands for it and that light’s colour is the pattern’s mean chroma; a genuinely two-hue front would need two registered lights (not now). The multi-hue can rows are gone. Where a design wants a second hue (the roundel’s red wedge below) it is plain albedo, not emission.

The restyle — a red machine and a blue one, “in spirit and with our art style”

From the maintainer’s reference photos. Shared structure: a full-height single-hue BACKLIT front on the coarse lattice (18 × 29 / 16 × 29 cells) with a black cap and frame; a dark CONTROL COLUMN inset on the right quarter (base lattice, NOT emissive: navy field, the bill / coin unit near the top with a black mouth, seven light-grey selection buttons each with a muted label chip to its left, the coin-return recess with a light lip); the DISPENSER as a real recess — each machine is now an upper body on a black plinth set 6 cm back over its left two-thirds plus a flush block under the column (+3 boxes a machine, 772 → 776; footprint and height unchanged, so nav and collision are untouched), the recess’s back wall marked black with a flap bar. Machine 1 (red): a red field, ONE white motif = the diagonal ribbon (a 3-cell band with a slight S, walked as a 3 × 3 stamp so it stays continuous however steep) from the lower left of the upper two-thirds to the top right, three white blocks of varied widths stepping up the open field beside it (the vertical wordmark, suggested — no letters); palette red (emit) · white (emit, 2.2 × the luminance, same warm cast) · black (no emission). Machine 2 (blue): a deep-blue field on a near-black navy body (the transparent cap / frame cells show it), a 9-cell ROUNDEL in the upper third — white ring and wave band, the upper wedge RED IN ALBEDO ONLY, the lower wedge the field’s blue — and four white blocks under it; palette blue (emit) · white (emit) · red (albedo). Both calibrated as before: the field’s LUMINOUS intensity = the old slab’s × VENDING_FLUX_K (1.0), one light each, coloured its mean: A I₀ 2.48 over 1.305 m² (colour 1 / 0.26 / 0.21), B 1.91 over 1.16 m² (0.23 / 0.37 / 1). Recipes: markingDefaults.ts vendingRedMarks / vendingBlueMarks (ribbonField, globeField, controlColumn, dispenserMarks); bodies in officeGen’s vending block.

Honest: at the old slabs’ luminous intensity the fields render as pale as the old slabs did (salmon / powder blue) — AgX desaturates radiance ≈ 2 at this exposure; the roundel’s red wedge, unlit in a dark room, reads near-black (a Pepsi globe by moonlight does too). VENDING_FLUX_K ≈ 0.5 gives a properly red / blue front in a break room half as bright — one constant, the maintainer’s call. The white blocks are blocks: letters wait for the SDF-glyph follow-up.

(i) Their image in the lino — before / after, high and ultra (night, fronts lit; ×3)

The lino’s finish is the real lever (physics, not the fix) — the same frame with the floor at 0.22 / 0.15 / 0.10

One number in officeGen OFFICE_FINISH.lino; it also sharpens every ceiling panel and torch in the corridor and break-room floors, which is why 0.22 was chosen in the RT-reflections lane. Parked as a taste call, not changed.

(ii) The keyboard in the manager’s dark screen (rough 0.08) — before / after, high and ultra (×3)

The desk laminate (rough 0.5‥0.6) is over every tier’s traced range but ultra’s edge, so “in the desk’s surface” has no reflection to show — by the finish table, not by the markings. The papers sit outside the screen’s mirror frustum from any camera that also sees the keyboard in it.

(iii) Marked cartons on the lobby stone (0.15) — night, a stand-in torch (a 40-cd spot where a guard would hold one), before / after, high and ultra (×3)

By day the same cartons mirror nothing visible in sunlit stone (captured, not shown: a dark face over a bright floor at F ≈ 0.04 is below the eye) — physically right, and a reminder that “shows in reflections” needs the reflected thing lit.

11. Honest read, object by object — what still doesn't read, and what reads as painted

  • Keyboard — reads. Two rows of keys is fewer than a keyboard has (five); the base lattice cannot do more in 14 cm and the maintainer asked for base. If it ever bothers anyone, fine caps (five rows) read up close and become a grey slab with a light middle at follow height — the same as verylow today. The mirrored keys in the dark monitor are a happy accident of §10 worth keeping.
  • Cartons — read, on the strength of the brown tape. The fine print is close-camera detail (said above); the shipping label on the far face is rarely seen from the follow camera (it faces away on most cartons) — harmless. Nothing reads as painted: tape and print are what cartons have. In an unlit corner (the cubicle stack by moonlight) nothing reads, correctly.
  • Vending machines — RESTYLED on 08-10 to the maintainer’s references (§10b: a red ribbon machine and a blue roundel machine, single-chroma emissive fields, dark control columns, recessed dispensers); they read instantly at follow height. Honest costs: the fields are as pale as the old slabs at the same flux (AgX at radiance ≈ 2 — VENDING_FLUX_K is the one-constant taste call), the roundel’s albedo-red wedge is dark in a dark room, and the white blocks are blocks until the SDF-glyph follow-up gives them letters.
  • Filing cabinets — read (three drawers, pulls). Coarse seams are 5 cm dark lines: at ×3 they look drawn-on rather than a shadowed gap — which is the rule working as intended (no baked shadow); a real 3 mm gap would be invisible at 21 m.
  • Papers / notice sheets / certificate — read as documents. The scribble variant (sign-in book, whiteboard) is a pixel zigzag: fine up close, a faint smudge at follow height — kept for close cameras, as briefed.
  • Whiteboards — read as used boards. The blue block is one line short of touching a sticky note; nobody will notice.
  • Door leaves — the plates are correct and physically shaded, and therefore nearly invisible on a dark leaf in a dark corridor until a light finds their lower roughness. If "door" needed help (it doesn't: the frame and the leaf's swing say door), a lighter leaf paint would do more than any marking.
  • Extinguisher / cylinder / cabinet — the label bands work; the cabinet's hollow-square pictogram is a placeholder for a real extinguisher symbol (an SDF glyph, later).
  • Racks — LEDs read as before (that was the bar to clear); the vent grille is deliberately faint and mostly shows in the reflection of a torch — if it reads as 'painted mesh' to the maintainer, its two greys are one constant apart (rackMarks: 0.05 / 0.07) and can go.
  • Binders — marginal at follow height (2 px labels); fine up close. The book runs on the manager's shelves (spine seams + a label band) read better because they are bigger.
  • Monitors — left almost alone as asked: two UI bars a hair brighter than the screen glow on lit screens only; from the follow camera the screen is 4 px tall and the bars are not separable from it — they exist for the close camera and the mirror. Dark screens get nothing (their switchable would not gate the glow).
  • What is missing entirely: text and logos (never draw letters at this resolution — an SDF-glyph atlas keyed into the same table is the follow-up, not built), the storage floor's 45° hatching (off-lattice), anything on characters.

13. Drive it

  • URL: ?nomarkings (off from boot: nothing evaluated, no marking lights) · ?level=relief (main's office: the demotion pass off, no markings — the A/B 'before' and the identity reference) · ?levelFile=office-t20.json / office-t40.json (the world-resolution variants, fetched from the dev server's /levels/; nothing extra bundled but the relief file).
  • Tab ▸ Renderer — markings: on/off · lattice scale (a debug rescale; the level's cells were generated for 2.5 cm) · contrast · emissive × · markings in reflections · a stats line. Debug view 1 (albedo) shows the flat cells, 14 the RT term with the windows in it.
  • Console: __mark.summary() · __mark.set({ on, contrast, emissive, reflect }) · __mark.list(i) / __mark.art(i) (a static box's markings, as records / as ASCII art; no argument = the box under the cursor) · __mark.marked() · __mark.lights (what was registered) · __mark.stats. Pane harness: await import('/qa/legibility-harness.js') → __lg.go(view, 'follow'|'close'), .tiles, .costAB, .frame1 (views: keyboard cartons cartonsCub vending vendingRefl cabinets papers whiteboard door extinguisher racks binders lobbySign breakEast).
  • Authoring: src/scene/markingDefaults.ts (the recipes + ASCII art) → src/scene/officeGen.ts call sites ({ markings, demote, texel } options) → bun run tools/level-export.ts (+ --relief, --texel 0.02) → probes.ts level. Format: src/scene/markings.ts (types, validation, generators, stats, packing, the fold); GPU: src/render/shaders/markings.wgsl; the table + slot: scene/boxes.ts; lights: game.ts (the block after the fixture area lights); supply: lighting.ts (Box.markGain).
  • Text / logos later: an SDF-glyph atlas addressed from the same per-box table (a fourth entry kind), evaluated in the same three places — not built here.
